instances.label: Personal exposure monitoring study at a manufacturing or chemical plant: design a sampling strategy (similar exposure groups, sample sizes, NIOSH/OSHA methods), calibrate pumps, fit sampling trains in workers' breathing zones at shift start, follow and log tasks through the shift, recover and ship media to an accredited lab, run AIHA-style statistical analysis, write the study report.

Area / direct-reading survey study inside an industrial facility: walk-through characterization of a process, placement and operation of real-time instruments (PID, aerosol monitor, multi-gas meter, sound level meter/dosimeters) at chosen locations and times, spatial/temporal mapping of concentrations, comparison to OELs, analysis and written findings.

Engineering-control / ventilation effectiveness research at a plant: pre- and post-intervention testing of local exhaust hoods and enclosures — anemometer traverses at hood faces, smoke-tube visualization, tracer-gas or dust-tracer tests around operating machinery and in tight, cluttered spaces — plus analysis of whether the control reduced exposure, and report.

Bench/laboratory research in a research or product-safety lab: sampling-and-analytical method development and validation (spiked filters/sorbent tubes, extraction, GC/HPLC/ICP analysis, recovery and precision studies), small chamber emission tests, or PPE/product performance testing, with iterative experimental design, data analysis and write-up.

Field exposure research at a construction site or other mobile/outdoor worksite: silica, welding fume, diesel exhaust or heat-stress study on crews whose layout, tasks and weather change day to day; instrument placement amid active equipment, task-based sampling, observation logs, analysis and report.

instances.label: Routine periodic safety round through a manufacturing or process plant floor: walk fixed routes looking for leaks, spills, overheating equipment, abnormal noise/vibration, out-of-range gauges, blocked aisles or exits, missing PPE and damaged equipment; log each finding with photo/location and raise corrective work orders.

Comprehensive documented safety-compliance audit of a facility or department: measure machine-guarding openings and reach distances, verify lockout/tagout procedures and energy-isolation points, check electrical panel labeling and clearances, chemical storage segregation and SDS, ventilation and noise exposure, interview operators and supervisors, then write citations and negotiate corrective actions with management.

Hands-on inspection and functional testing of safety equipment: activate and flow-test emergency eyewashes/showers, check fire extinguisher gauges, pins, seals and tags, functionally test emergency stops, interlocks and light curtains, inspect fall-arrest harnesses, lanyards and ladders for defects, verify relief devices; tag or remove defective items from service and fix minor deficiencies on the spot.

Instrumented hazard survey inside an industrial facility: thermographic scanning of electrical gear and rotating machinery, ultrasonic/acoustic leak detection on compressed-air and process piping, and gas/vapor atmospheric monitoring around tank farms, process units and confined-space approaches, with a written survey report of hazardous readings.

Safety walk of an active construction or field site: identify fall hazards, unguarded holes and drop-offs, excavation and scaffold problems, blocked egress, housekeeping and debris, standing water, PPE non-use and equipment-pedestrian conflicts, on a layout that changes daily and in outdoor weather; issue observations and corrective directives to the crews.

instances.label: Desk-based review of building designs: architectural/MEP drawings, BIM models and sprinkler shop drawings checked against IBC/NFPA 13/14/101 to determine required suppression, detection and egress provisions, occupant loads, exit widths and travel distances, hydraulic demand; reviewer issues written comments back to the design team. Setting: engineering/consulting office; essentially no physical act beyond handling paper or a screen.

Walkthrough survey of an existing occupied commercial or institutional building (office tower, school, hotel, hospital): walk every floor and stairwell, check exit locations, path widths, door hardware and rated door labels, exit/emergency lighting, sprinkler head coverage and obstructions, standpipe and extinguisher locations, alarm devices, and unsealed penetrations above lay-in ceilings (lifting tiles, opening doors and closets); produce a deficiency list and system-upgrade recommendations against code.

Hazard survey of an operating industrial or high-piled-storage facility (warehouse, chemical plant, data center): classify commodities and storage arrangement, measure clearance to sprinklers and aisle widths, inspect special-hazard suppression (clean agent, foam, dust collection), control valves, fire pump room and hydrants, and identify ignition/exposure hazards; recommend protection scheme. Congested plant floors, mezzanines, ladders, PPE required.

Field inspection of a building under construction or renovation: verify installed firestopping and rated wall/floor assemblies before concealment, sprinkler piping and hanger installation, shaft and damper construction, temporary means of egress and hot-work controls; conditions are unfinished, cluttered with materials and trades, ladders/lifts needed, layout changes week to week.

Water supply evaluation: conduct or witness an NFPA 291 hydrant flow test on street or campus mains (remove caps, attach cap/pitot gauges, open and close hydrants, record static/residual/flow), inspect the fire pump and tanks, run a pump churn/flow test, then compute available supply versus sprinkler/standpipe demand for the building.

Assessment of small, atypical or uncontrolled sites: a private residence or small mixed-use structure, a historic building with non-standard construction, a temporary event venue or a remote/rural facility, where layout, access and construction materials must be taken as found and often verified by probing concealed construction.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous construction-site inspection/documentation. It shows a robot can traverse the same unstructured settings a fire engineer visits, but the delivered output is imagery/maps for humans, not a determination of fire protection requirements, so it does not substantiate completion of this task.

sources.title: AI Startup Using Robots and Lidar to Boost Productivity on Construction Sites - IEEE Spectrum

sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated as-built verification against a design model on construction sites — the closest existing automation to 'inspect the building against the design'. It verifies installed geometry only and does not evaluate fire protection requirements, so it cannot complete this task.

sources.title: Cobalt security robot to protect your people and places
sources.claim: Cobalt's indoor robot autonomously patrols offices and other indoor facilities on routes, flagging anomalies (open doors, leaks, unusual objects) with remote human specialists reviewing events; it performs anomaly flagging, not a code-based fire protection survey.

sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial plant inspection rounds. Same class of facility a fire protection engineer surveys, but readings are limited to pre-taught asset checkpoints (thermal, vibration, gas); it does not assess storage arrangement, sprinkler adequacy or code compliance.

instances.label: Origin-and-cause examination of a burned commercial or industrial building for an insurer, owner, or litigation: move through a fire-damaged, partly collapsed, soot- and water-fouled structure; document burn, char, and V-patterns; hand-excavate and layer debris in the suspected area of origin; recover and preserve artifacts (appliance, wiring, gas piping, sprinkler head); form and test ignition hypotheses; state what would have prevented the loss (sprinklers, compartmentation, housekeeping, ignition-source control).

Residential, small-occupancy, vehicle/equipment or exterior/wildland-interface fire scene: same origin-and-cause work in a burned dwelling or open yard, weather-exposed, debris and contents as found, no institution controlling the site; conclude cause and preventable factors (e.g., extension cord, dryer lint, unattended cooking, defective battery).

Post-incident investigation inside an operating, institution-controlled facility after a contained fire (plant, warehouse, data center, hospital): examine the involved equipment in place, pull alarm/BMS/SCADA and maintenance records, inspect and flow/trip-test the sprinkler and detection systems that operated, interview operators, and determine both the ignition cause and why the protection under-performed.

Desk analysis at the engineer's office: review fire department incident reports, scene photographs and 3D scans, witness statements, product recall and maintenance history, alarm data; run hand calculations or CFD/FDS fire modeling to test competing hypotheses; issue the cause determination and prevention recommendations.

Laboratory or test-facility work: bench examination and disassembly of recovered artifacts (X-ray/CT, microscopy, arc mapping of conductors, teardown of a failed appliance or battery pack), submission and interpretation of fire debris samples, or exemplar/reconstruction burn testing to confirm or exclude an ignition scenario.

Institution-controlled premises, fixed layout, standard equipment.

Office / administrative area assessment: ergonomist walks cubicles and shared spaces, evaluates individual computer workstations (chair, monitor height, keyboard/mouse reach, glare), interviews occupants about discomfort, and notes cord/trip hazards and blocked aisles; produces per-workstation findings and recommendations.

Warehouse, distribution center or retail back-of-house inspection: aisles, dock doors, pallet racking, order-picking stations; checks for floor spills and debris, obstructed walkways and exits, damaged racking, lift-truck traffic conflicts and heavy lifting/reaching hazards; documents hazards for corrective action.

Healthcare, laboratory or clinical service area inspection: occupied patient units, labs or kitchens; observes patient-handling and transfer tasks, checks lift equipment availability, clutter and slip hazards in corridors and rooms, sharps and storage reach heights; documents hazards while working around staff and patients.

Field / outdoor site visit: construction jobsite, utility yard, transportation or mining site taken as found - uneven terrain, changing layout, weather, heavy equipment and multiple trades; inspects for fall, struck-by, terrain and manual-handling hazards and issues a site hazard report.

instances.label: Office/computer-workstation ergonomic evaluation: engineer goes to an employee's cubicle in a corporate office, interviews the worker, observes seated posture, works through a checklist, measures desk/monitor/keyboard heights, seat pan and reach distances with a tape or ruler, physically adjusts the chair/monitor arm, and writes up findings and recommendations.

Manufacturing or distribution-center job task and physical demands analysis: on the plant/DC floor the engineer videotapes workers on the line, decomposes the job into task elements and cycle times, weighs parts and totes on a scale, measures push/pull forces on carts, doors, levers and hand tools with a push-pull force gauge, measures heights and reaches, then scores the job (NIOSH lifting index, REBA/RULA) and reports.

Anthropometric measurement of a subject population for design/fit (PPE, uniforms, cockpit, seat, tool sizing): dozens of human subjects are measured at an institution-controlled measuring station with tape, calipers, sitting-height stand or 3D scanner; landmarks are palpated/marked, dimensions recorded and statistically summarized.

Laboratory human-factors evaluation with human participants: participants perform representative tasks on a device, simulator or mock-up while the engineer sets up and runs video recording, instruments controls and seats with sensors, times task steps, and administers workload/usability questionnaires.

Field analysis in unstructured settings: construction sites, patient rooms and home care, utility/field crews, farms or vehicles. The engineer videotapes work as found, applies observational checklists, and takes in-situ force, weight and dimension measurements amid clutter, weather, moving equipment and non-standard layouts.

Bench force/fit measurement of a fixtured product or workstation mock-up with no human participant: a sample (control panel, latch, lever, seat, hand-tool interface) is clamped in a test lab and the engineer applies loads at defined contact points, records force-displacement data, and reports it against human strength/comfort criteria.

instances.label: Production-floor physical-agent survey in a manufacturing plant: the ergonomist walks a taught set of workstations during production carrying a sound level meter with octave-band filters, a WBGT heat-stress meter, a light meter and a thermoanemometer, holding each instrument at the operator's ear/task/breathing-zone position, waiting for readings to stabilize, and logging values by location.

Indoor workplace/office environmental and workstation assessment (offices, control rooms, labs, hospital units): illuminance readings at desks and task surfaces, air velocity at diffusers and workstations, temperature/humidity (sling psychrometer or electronic psychrometer), background noise levels, plus inclinometer readings on chair backs, monitor stands and work surfaces.

Human-factors laboratory motion-analysis session: set up and calibrate the optical/IMU motion capture volume (wand calibration), apply reflective markers or strap IMU/EMG sensors to a human participant's anatomical landmarks, run recorded trials with instructed movements, and check data quality before releasing the participant.

In-plant/warehouse instrumentation of real workers: fitting inclinometers/IMU posture sensors, dosimeters or heart-rate monitors onto an operator, verifying placement and orientation, capturing data during a live work shift on the floor, then removing and downloading the devices.

Outdoor or field-site measurement round (construction site, utility yard, agricultural site, confined-space entry): heat-stress meter set up near workers, sling psychrometer whirled for wet-bulb readings, colorimetric detection tubes drawn with a bellows pump for contaminant screening, plus light and air-velocity spot checks, in changing weather and terrain.

instances.label: Pre-/post-study calibration verification of the validation sensor fleet in the company's validation/metrology lab: bundling 20-100 thermocouples/RTDs or wireless data loggers, connecting them to the validator (Kaye/Ellab type), immersing the bundle in an ice point and dry-block/bath, running the automated verification at setpoints, reviewing pass/fail against tolerance, tagging and filing the record.

Making up new sensor lead and cable assemblies for upcoming studies: cutting thermocouple/extension wire to length, stripping, forming or welding junctions, fitting connectors and strain reliefs, ID-labeling each lead, and continuity/loop checking before it enters the kit.

Inspecting and repairing damaged items in the validation kit at the bench: chasing an intermittent or open channel, cutting back and re-terminating a crushed lead, replacing kinked or bent probes, cleaning probe tips, connectors and sensor housings, insulation/loop resistance checks.

Running the calibration/maintenance program for the equipment pool: pulling instruments that are coming due from production suites, warehouse and cabinets, applying or updating calibration status labels, segregating out-of-tolerance or damaged units into quarantine, packing and shipping units to the accredited external cal lab, receiving them back, checking certificates and restocking.

Bench troubleshooting and servicing of validation instruments: a data logger that will not boot or hold charge, a failed input module or fuse, battery and desiccant replacement, firmware/software upgrade and post-service functional check, or preparing the unit and fault description for vendor depot repair.

In-situ maintenance of installed or bulky validation test equipment on the production floor / GMP suite: wiping down and sanitizing wireless loggers and sensor bundles between runs, replacing tubing, filters, gaskets or isokinetic probes on leak testers and particle counters, checking fixed reference probes and test rigs in place, restoring the rig after a study.

tasks.label: Conduct validation or qualification tests of new or existing processes, equipment, or software in accordance with internal protocols or external standards.

instances.label: GMP equipment/utility qualification in an operating pharma or biotech plant: IQ/OQ/PQ of an autoclave, lyophilizer, depyrogenation tunnel, HVAC system or WFI loop — placing thermocouples and biological indicators in worst-case chamber/load positions, verifying installed instrumentation and connections, running cycles, taking utility samples, and compiling the executed qualification package with deviations.

Cleanroom/aseptic-area classification and environmental qualification rounds: walking a defined route through Grade A-D rooms taking non-viable particle counts and viable active-air samples at protocol-defined locations, labeling and transferring plates, and logging timestamped results against acceptance criteria.

Process performance qualification and cleaning validation on a production line (fill-finish, tablet press, blender, CIP/SIP train): pulling stratified in-process samples during PPQ batches, performing in-process checks, swabbing equipment surfaces at defined sampling points, reconciling yields, and documenting the executed batch protocol.

Product, component or materials qualification bench testing in a test lab: mounting specimens or devices (packaging seals, autoinjector parts, metal/plastic coupons, touch panels, control modules) in test rigs and chambers, running tensile/peel/fatigue/cycle or HMI test suites to ASTM, ISO or certification-body protocols, and reporting results against criteria.

Vehicle or system-level validation testing at a test facility: executing durability, misuse, mileage-accumulation or emissions drive-cycle schedules on a proving ground track or chassis dynamometer, with instrumented data capture over long, repetitive test programs.

Computer system / software validation at a workstation: executing scripted IQ/OQ/PQ test cases against an MES, LIMS or instrument software build, capturing screenshots and evidence, recording pass/fail and discrepancies in the validation record.

Solid-dose / finished-unit sampling during validation runs: pulling tablets, capsules, filled vials or packaged units at defined intervals or locations from a tablet press, blender, capsule filler or fill-finish/packaging line (including stratified and start/middle/end sampling) into labeled sample containers.

Incoming raw material / component sampling in a warehouse sampling booth or dispensary: opening drums, bags or totes of powders and liquids, using a sample thief or scoop on a defined number of containers, transferring material into labeled sample jars/vials and reclosing containers.

Cleaning-validation sampling: swabbing protocol-defined worst-case locations on cleaned equipment (tank and mixer interiors, hoses, filling parts, sometimes disassembled) with wetted swabs and collecting final-rinse samples, placing each swab in a labeled extraction tube for the lab.

Environmental monitoring sampling during cleanroom qualification, media fill or aseptic process simulation: viable active air samples, settle plates and surface samples taken along a mapped route through classified rooms, with plates identified and sent to micro.

Utility sampling during water/gas system validation: drawing purified water and WFI samples from every use point on the loop over consecutive days, plus clean steam condensate and compressed gas samples, into sterile sample bottles per protocol.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Periodic life-saving appliance check aboard a merchant vessel alongside at a terminal (class/flag surveyor, port-state officer, or fleet superintendent): walk the boat deck and muster stations, open LSA lockers, count and condition-check lifejackets, immersion suits, pyrotechnics and EPIRB/SART, verify liferaft service tags and hydrostatic release expiry, hands-on inspection of davits, falls, brakes and on-load release gear, witness a lifeboat lowering and crew drill, then write up deficiencies against SOLAS Ch. III.

Pollution-prevention (MARPOL) equipment check in the machinery spaces of a vessel at berth: climb through a hot, cluttered engine room and bilge areas, functionally test the oily-water separator and 15 ppm bilge alarm, trace overboard piping and flanges for unauthorized bypasses, sound sludge/bilge tanks and reconcile against the Oil Record Book, check incinerator, sewage plant, ballast water treatment system and scrubber washwater monitoring, and log findings.

Verification at a shipyard during newbuilding or drydock repair: check installed lifeboat/liferaft arrangements, launching appliances, escape routes, MARPOL tank protection, OWS and BWTS installations against approved plans and rule requirements, witness davit load tests and equipment commissioning amid scaffolding, staging, hot work and shifting site conditions.

Monitoring under way — riding the ship on a voyage or sea trial: observe operation of pollution-control machinery and emissions in a seaway, witness abandon-ship and pollution-response drills at sea, check that equipment functions with vessel motion, noise and weather, and report to owner/administration.

External surveillance of ships' emissions and discharges for a maritime administration: screen passing or berthed vessels for MARPOL Annex VI fuel-sulphur compliance and for oil/discharge violations from shore, boat or aircraft over a busy coastal traffic lane or harbour, identify vessels and pass suspected non-compliance to inspectors for follow-up.

Office-based fleet compliance monitoring: review certificates and survey status, scanned Oil Record Book pages, continuous emission and OWS alarm logs, planned-maintenance records for LSA, and remote-survey video from crew; flag non-conformities and schedule corrective action.

tasks.label: Check, test, and maintain automatic controls and alarm systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Commissioning / builder's and sea trials on a newly built or overhauled vessel at a shipyard: the engineer works through the machinery-space alarm and automation test matrix — physically simulating low lube-oil pressure, high jacket-water temperature, bilge high level, tank levels; jumpering or heating sensors; verifying annunciation on the engine control room console and bridge extension, automatic standby-pump start, slowdowns/shutdowns, blackout recovery — with a class surveyor witnessing. Spaces are crowded with staging, temporary cabling and other trades; systems are partly incomplete and punch-listed.

Periodic in-service testing aboard an operating deep-sea vessel (annual survey, UMS/unattended machinery space certification, monthly drills): functional test of fire and smoke detection loops with test aerosol/heat, bilge and tank high-level float switches, engineers' dead-man alarm, general alarm, machinery safety trips and the alarm-monitoring computer; walking hot, vibrating, ladder-connected machinery spaces and logging pass/fail for each point.

Routine bench work in a shop, calibration lab or land-based engineering site: scheduled calibration and functional (stimulus-response) verification of pressure/temperature transmitters and switches, level switches and portable/fixed gas detectors used in alarm circuits; documented as-found/as-left records against a known standard.

Bench diagnosis and repair of a faulty controller or alarm module returned from a vessel: unknown fault, tracing wiring and I/O with a meter, reseating/replacing components, reflashing or re-parameterising the controller, then re-testing and signing off.

Onboard fault diagnosis and corrective maintenance in service: an intermittent or spurious alarm traced to a corroded connector, salt-fouled detector, drifted transmitter or failed relay in a cramped, hot, vibrating machinery space or void; component cleaned/replaced/recalibrated, setpoint adjusted, system retested and the log annotated.

Work on small craft, workboats, ferries, dredges, research vessels and offshore units at a pier or small yard: aging, undocumented, one-off alarm and control installations that differ vessel to vessel; testing and patching up monitoring panels, alarm horns, engine safety circuits with limited drawings and awkward access.

tasks.label: Evaluate operation of marine equipment during acceptance testing and shakedown cruises.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Builder's sea trial of a newly built commercial vessel (containership, tanker, ferry, offshore support vessel): engineer sails for several days, works the engine room and machinery control room during full-power, endurance, maneuvering, crash-stop and astern runs; takes and cross-checks temperatures, pressures, shaft power/torsionmeter, vibration and noise measurements, walks rounds feeling and looking for leaks, hot bearings and abnormal noise, judges whether propulsion and auxiliary machinery meet contract performance, and logs deficiencies for the yard. Cramped, hot, noisy machinery spaces on a rolling deck.

Harbor/dockside acceptance testing at the shipyard pier before delivery: engineer runs installed systems through written test protocols with the vendor and class surveyor – diesel generators on load banks, steering gear hard-over timing, bow thruster, fire and bilge pumps, HVAC, alarm and safety-trip/shutdown verification, blackout and emergency start tests – verifies readings against specification, witnesses trips, and endorses or rejects each test sheet.

Shop/factory acceptance test of major marine machinery at the manufacturer's test facility (main engine, reduction gearbox, large genset) mounted on an instrumented test bed with a water brake or dynamometer: engineer witnesses the load-step and overspeed/safety-device program alongside the class surveyor, reviews performance and emissions data against the specification, participates in post-run opening inspection (crankcase, bearings, crankshaft deflections), judges deviations and signs the shop test report.

Bench acceptance testing of serially produced marine auxiliary equipment at a supplier's test facility (centrifugal and screw pumps, electric motors, small gensets, valves, coolers): unit fixtured on an instrumented test stand, run through fixed duty points, performance/leak/vibration data compared against a fixed acceptance specification, pass/fail decision and test certificate issued.

Naval vessel builder's trials, acceptance trials and post-delivery shakedown (e.g., INSURV-style trials on a destroyer, auxiliary or submarine): multi-day at-sea evaluation of propulsion plant, electric plant, steering, damage-control and auxiliary systems including casualty and degraded-condition drills, with a large trial team, scripted trial agenda, deficiency (starred card) lists and formal acceptance recommendations.

Small craft and in-service vessel testing: sea trial of a tug, workboat, patrol boat or yacht run out of a private marina or small boatyard in open water (checking engine load curve, bollard pull, steering, vibration in a cramped engine compartment), or commissioning/acceptance testing of retrofitted or overhauled equipment (scrubber, ballast water treatment system, rebuilt main engine) aboard an operating ship in a repair yard cluttered with staging, hoses and cabling.

sources.title: BP deploys robot on offshore oil rig to enhance safety - SAFETY4SEA
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot has been deployed on bp's Mad Dog platform in the Gulf of Mexico performing operator rounds – reading gauges, ..., sniffing for methane and identifying leaks – on preset autonomous inspection routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine machinery inspection rounds on an offshore production facility. roles.description: Design, evaluate, modify, or construct fuel cell components or systems for transportation, stationary, or portable applications.

tasks.label: Plan or conduct experiments to validate new materials, optimize startup protocols, reduce conditioning time, or examine contaminant tolerance.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Single-cell validation campaign for a new material (catalyst-coated membrane, ionomer, GDL): cut/align components on the lab bench, assemble the 5-50 cm2 test cell hardware and torque it, mount it on a hydrogen-rated test station, plumb and leak-check, run break-in plus polarization/EIS diagnostics, then disassemble and inspect. R&D fuel-cell laboratory.

Startup/shutdown and conditioning-protocol experiments on an existing single cell or short stack: define a matrix of current/voltage/RH/temperature/purge profiles aimed at shortening break-in time or improving cold/freeze start, run many cycles unattended on an automated test bench (sometimes inside an environmental chamber), compare recovery and performance, iterate on the protocol. Lab test cell/bench.

Contaminant-tolerance test: dose ppm-level CO, H2S, NH3, SO2 or air-side contaminants into reactant streams of an installed cell, hold for tens-to-hundreds of hours with periodic diagnostics and recovery steps, log and interpret degradation. Lab test station with gas blending/injection hardware.

Ex-situ materials validation and screening: synthesize or receive candidate catalyst/support/membrane samples, formulate and disperse inks, coat or drop-cast electrodes, run half-cell/RDE electrochemistry and characterization (SEM, XRD, porosimetry), iterate compositions. Chemistry/electrochemistry bench in the same R&D facility.

Experiments on novel prototype hardware or system-level rigs: instrument a one-off short stack, balance-of-plant skid, or vehicle-mounted system with thermocouples, pressure taps and sensors; build ad-hoc plumbing; run startup protocols under realistic conditions and troubleshoot leaks, fittings and sensor faults as they arise. Institution-controlled test cell or partner facility, but the rig itself is unique and improvised.

Plan-only instance: design the test matrix/DOE and acceptance criteria for a materials-validation or contaminant study, write the protocol and safety review, then analyze the returned data and report; execution is delegated to technicians. Engineer's desk/office within the lab facility.

System- or vehicle-level and field testing: fuel cell system installed in a vehicle, a container, or a stationary site; engineer connects portable analyzers and data loggers, runs performance and diagnostic sequences under ambient/real-world conditions and troubleshoots on site.

instances.label: A field-returned or endurance-tested PEM stack / short stack arrives at the OEM engineering test lab. The engineer defines a diagnostic plan, installs the stack on a fuel cell test station (gas, coolant, load, cell-voltage harness), and runs polarization curves, EIS/HFR, hydrogen-crossover and pressure-decay leak checks, cell-voltage mapping, then interprets the data to characterize the degradation/failure mode.

Teardown of the returned stack/module on a lab bench: releasing tie rods and end plates, de-stacking hundreds of thin bipolar plates, MEAs and gaskets without destroying evidence, per-cell visual inspection for pinholes, delamination, corrosion, coolant leaks and seal damage, photographic documentation and selection of samples for further analysis.

Post-service analysis of a failed balance-of-plant electromechanical component returned from the field (air blower/compressor, coolant pump, solenoid or purge valve, hydrogen injector, sensor, contactor, wiring harness/connector): functional run on a component rig, electrical measurements (continuity, insulation, current signature), vibration/noise checks, then disassembly and inspection to identify the fault mechanism.

On-site investigation of a failed fielded system — a stationary fuel cell genset at a customer's plant/hospital/data-center pad, or an FCEV bus or truck in a fleet depot service bay: downloading controller logs, opening cabinets, tracing electrical faults with meters and scopes, hydrogen leak and thermal surveys, testing or swapping suspect components, and confirming root cause in situ.

Materials/microstructural characterization of samples extracted from failed hardware: sectioning MEA/bipolar-plate/seal specimens, mounting, grinding and polishing, optical and SEM-EDS imaging, identification of contamination particles, catalyst-layer thinning, Pt bands, coating loss or corrosion products, written into the failure report.

instances.label: R&D lab bench: engineer builds up a single-cell or short-stack test fixture with a new MEA/GDL, torques the compression bolts, mounts it on the fuel cell test station, connects anode/cathode gas lines (compression fittings), coolant lines, current collector cables, thermocouples and cell-voltage taps, then leak-checks and purges before the test.

Lab/test facility: preparing and verifying the station's instrumentation for a specific test — installing or swapping mass flow controllers, pressure transducers, humidifier and back-pressure hardware, checking/zeroing sensors against reference standards, ranging the electronic load, and documenting calibration.

Lab/test facility: setting up the data acquisition system for the planned test — landing sensor and voltage-tap leads on DAQ terminal blocks/connectors, configuring channels, scaling, sample rates, safety limits and alarm interlocks in the test software, and verifying live signals before the run.

Test high-bay or system test cell: preparing a bench for a full-size stack or vehicle/stationary fuel cell system — staging the unit, connecting hydrogen supply, air handling, coolant loop and high-current cables to the load bank, hooking up H2 detectors, ventilation and safety interlocks, then pressure/leak testing and purging.

Field/on-site: instrumenting a deployed fuel cell unit (bus, forklift, backup power unit) at a customer or demo site — routing and securing sensor cables in a non-standard layout, mounting a portable DAQ, tapping vehicle CAN/power, and verifying signals under site conditions.

tasks.label: Develop fuel cell materials or fuel cell test equipment.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: R&D lab bench work developing candidate fuel cell materials: weighing catalyst powders and supports, dispensing solvents/ionomer, mixing/sonicating inks or polymer solutions, curing/annealing samples, and running a comparative screen across a formulation matrix to pick the best candidates. Standard institutional materials/chemistry lab with fume hoods, balances, hot plates, glovebox.

Ex-situ characterization and performance screening of the candidate materials: polishing glassy-carbon RDE tips, drop-casting catalyst films, running ORR/HER cyclic voltammetry and durability cycling on a potentiostat, conductivity or ex-situ membrane tests, and reducing the data into activity/stability rankings. Institutional electrochemistry lab.

Fabricating prototype test hardware from the materials: coating/cutting membranes and gas diffusion layers, hot-pressing MEAs, stacking gaskets, bipolar plates and end plates into a single cell or short stack, torqueing to spec, leak-checking and mounting it on a test station for in-situ evaluation. Lab or pilot-line area.

Developing custom fuel cell test equipment: building and commissioning a bespoke test stand or fixture - cutting and routing gas/coolant tubing and compression fittings, mounting mass flow controllers, humidifier, heaters, valves and sensors on a frame, wiring the electronic load, DAQ and safety interlocks, integrating control software, then leak-checking, calibrating and debugging until it produces trustworthy data. Lab test bay / engineering shop.

Desk-based development work: DFT or continuum modelling of candidate materials, CAD and P&ID design of test hardware, writing specifications and test plans, selecting vendor components, and analyzing/reporting results. Office within the engineering facility; no physical handling.

tasks.label: Fabricate prototypes of fuel cell components, assemblies, stacks, or systems.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Build a prototype PEM stack on a bench in a company R&D lab or prototype assembly room: sequence and align dozens to hundreds of bipolar plates, sub-gasketed MEAs, gaskets, current collectors and end plates on alignment rods, then compress to a target load and torque tie rods, and leak/insulation check the finished stack.

Fabricate individual prototype hardware in the lab machine shop / rapid-prototyping area: CNC-mill graphite or metal flow-field plates, machine aluminum end plates, manifolds and compression fixtures, die- or laser-cut gaskets and sub-gaskets to a new drawing, deburr and inspect.

Fabricate electrode / catalyst-coated-membrane prototypes in a lab fume hood or coating bench: mix and sonicate catalyst ink, spray or slot-die coat the membrane or GDL, dry, hot-press/decal-transfer into a 5- or 7-layer MEA, and cut to size.

Integrate a complete prototype fuel cell system or test rig in a lab high-bay: mount the stack in a frame or enclosure, route and cut flexible hydrogen/air/coolant lines, make up compression and push-to-connect fittings, install blower, humidifier, valves, pumps and sensors, wire the harness, DC-DC and controller, then leak- and hi-pot-test.

Rework and modify an existing prototype at the bench: disassemble a stack to swap a failed MEA or leaking gasket, re-shim and re-torque, retrofit a redesigned plate or seal, repair a wire or fitting found during testing, working with hand tools around a partly built one-off article.

instances.label: Underground working-section / development-heading examination (coal or hard rock): walk the face area and travelways, take methane/CO/O2 and air-quantity readings at set locations, sound and assess roof and ribs, check installed ground support, ventilation curtains and stoppings, check face equipment and permissibility, then record hazards, date-time-initial the exam and post or correct dangerous conditions.

Routine inspection of fixed underground infrastructure along established roadways: main belt conveyor entries (idlers, alignment, hot bearings, spillage, fire protection), pump stations, electrical substations, shaft/hoist landings and refuge stations — a fixed-layout, institution-controlled underground area with standard equipment.

Inspection of inaccessible or freshly blasted underground areas: open stopes and voids, orepasses and chutes, old workings, and headings shortly after a blast — checking void geometry, overbreak, hangups, loose ground and re-entry gas conditions, in places people are barred from entering.

Geotechnical inspection of surface pit walls: highwall faces and crests, bench widths and catch berms, waste dumps and spoil piles — looking for tension cracks, movement, ravelling and loose material, typically on a scheduled cycle and after blasting or heavy rain.

General surface workplace examination of the active pit: drive/walk the pit floor, working faces, ramps and haul roads, dumps, loadout and stockpile areas; check road berms and grades, water and mud, spill and rockfall hazards, guarding, access ladders, signage, and the condition of mobile equipment in service; record adverse conditions and corrections.

Inspection of fixed surface facilities: crushing and screening plant, conveyor galleries and transfer points, prep plant, wash plant, shops, electrical rooms and hoist house — checking guards, hot bearings, belt condition, leaks, housekeeping, walkways and handrails inside a controlled, standard-layout industrial facility.

instances.label: Routine underground air-quality/ventilation survey round in an active metal or coal mine: the engineer travels a circuit of stations (intakes, working sections, ramps, returns, refuge stations), takes multi-gas readings (CO, NO2, CH4, O2, H2S) plus airflow readings, records them against statutory limits, and calls for ventilation adjustments (regulator settings, auxiliary fan/duct changes, brattice) where readings approach limits. Muck piles, water, mobile equipment traffic and a layout that changes as the mine advances.

Pre-entry / re-entry gas check of a specific area before crews go back in: a freshly blasted development heading full of blast fumes (CO, NO2), an inaccessible stope, ore pass or old working, or an area after a diesel/battery incident. The engineer or their designee must confirm the atmosphere is clear or specify additional ventilation/waiting time before entry.

Sealed-area, goaf/gob and bleeder atmosphere monitoring in a gassy coal mine: sampling behind seals via sample pipes/boreholes and from fixed monitoring points, bag samples analysed by gas chromatograph, computing spontaneous-combustion indicator ratios and explosibility, and advising on inertisation, seal integrity or ventilation change.

Air testing rounds at fixed mine facilities on surface or at shaft/plant infrastructure: processing plant and reagent areas (H2S, SO2, LEL), fan houses, shaft stations, battery-charging and pump rooms, silos and bins prior to entry; readings taken on a repeatable route in an institution-controlled, fixed-layout industrial facility, with recommendations for local exhaust or added ventilation.

Emergency or post-incident atmosphere assessment: after a mine fire, explosion, inrush or heating, sampling through boreholes and remaining monitoring lines, tracking gas trends in an irrespirable and possibly collapsed atmosphere, and advising on re-entry, inertisation or ventilation changes.

Engineering study work: a mine-wide ventilation survey campaign (gas and airflow measurements at many stations over days) feeding a ventilation network model, producing a design recommendation such as a new ventilation shaft, raise, booster fan or main-fan upgrade for a mine expansion or a tunnelling project.

instances.label: Bench-scale aqueous chemistry campaign in a fume hood or glovebox at a national-lab/university radiological lab: solvent-extraction distribution-ratio study, batch sorption test, or waste-form leach test using surrogates or tracer-level radionuclides. Dozens to hundreds of repeat conditions: solution make-up, phase contacting, separation, aliquoting, ICP-MS/gamma analysis, iterate on results.

Waste-form or fuel-material synthesis and screening with non-radioactive surrogates: weigh and mix oxide/glass-frit/grout batches, melt or heat-treat in furnaces, quench, crush, characterize by XRD/SEM/thermal analysis, and iterate formulation to meet durability or processability targets. Standard chemistry/materials lab.

Bespoke bench rig experiment: engineer builds or modifies one-off apparatus (molten-salt electrorefining cell in an argon glovebox, high-temperature furnace with off-gas train, corrosion autoclave, gas-evolution or thermal rig), instruments it with thermocouples/electrodes, runs the test with in-run troubleshooting, then disassembles and recovers specimens.

Hot cell / shielded-cell experiment on irradiated fuel or high-activity material: receive an irradiated segment, section it with remote saws, dissolve fuel or run separations, prepare metallographic mounts, transfer between in-cell stations using master-slave manipulators, and recover samples for assay. Every specimen unique, contamination control critical.

Instrumented measurement/NDE campaign on already-prepared specimens of irradiated material inside a shielded glovebox or hot cell: load specimens into thermophysical-property, gamma-scan, profilometry, XRD or microscopy instruments, run the standard measurement sequence per the exam plan, and log qualified data.

Pilot/engineering-scale or field test: run a pilot melter, centrifugal-contactor cascade, calciner, or dry-storage/canister corrosion demonstration campaign; or a field/in-situ disposal test (lysimeters, borehole or underground-research-lab experiments). Install and align the rig, operate it over days to months, take process samples, and tear it down.

sources.developer: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / UC Berkeley
sources.title: An autonomous laboratory for the accelerated synthesis of inorganic materials | Nature
sources.claim: The A-Lab is an autonomous robotic platform that plans, executes and interprets solid-state synthesis experiments (powder dosing, furnace heat treatment, robotic transfers, XRD characterization) in a closed loop inside an enclosed automated laboratory.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous inorganic powder synthesis and characterization. Transfers to surrogate waste-form/fuel-material screening because the objects (weighed oxide powders, crucibles, furnace runs, XRD coupons) and precision are the same class of work; a 2026 C&EN report notes a correction to the paper's phase-identification claims, not to the robotic execution.

sources.title: A mobile robotic chemist | Nature
sources.claim: A free-roaming mobile robot ran an eight-day closed-loop experimental campaign of 688 photocatalysis experiments in a conventional chemistry laboratory, choosing conditions by Bayesian search.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous non-radioactive photocatalyst screening in a human-configured lab. It shows autonomous multi-day experiment campaigns are possible, but there is no demonstration in a radiological/glovebox lab, so it does not by itself substantiate radiochemical experiments at E2.

sources.system: Autonomous hot cell tool (Universal Robots UR3e arm) at INL's Irradiated Materials Characterization Laboratory
sources.title: Supporting innovation with automation: INL researcher develops autonomous hot cell tool - Idaho National Laboratory
sources.claim: An INL-developed robotic arm autonomously positions irradiated specimens inside a hot cell and a glovebox housing thermophysical-property instruments, selecting placement according to sample attributes and the examination being performed, replacing manipulator work for post-irradiation examination.

sources.system: Radiation-tolerant automated high pressure ion chromatography (HPIC) system
sources.title: Isotopes – Faster Ac-225 production | ORNL
sources.claim: ORNL built an automated high-pressure ion chromatography system that runs actinium-225 separation chemistry on dissolved irradiated thorium targets inside a hot cell, using radiation-tolerant pneumatic control instead of hands-on gravity separations by technicians.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated separation chemistry on irradiated targets. Transfers to fuel-reclamation separations experiments because the feed (dissolved irradiated actinide-bearing material), the chemistry (ion-exchange/extraction separation) and the shielded enclosure are the same class of work.

sources.system: Automated high-throughput liquid-liquid extraction instrument with Bayesian optimization
sources.title: LA-UR-24-31710 Accepted Manuscript (Los Alamos National Laboratory)
sources.claim: A LANL automated experimental instrument, steered by Bayesian optimization, executed a full high-throughput liquid-liquid extraction campaign for rare-earth/actinide (4f/5f) separations, running hundreds of distribution-ratio measurements and identifying optimal conditions without a full manual screen.
sources.transferJustification: This is the same class of experiment as the task's fuel-reclamation separations studies (f-element liquid-liquid extraction distribution ratios); the accepted manuscript corresponds to LANL work published as 'Advancing Rare-Earth (4f) and Actinide (5f) Separation through Machine Learning and Automated High-Throughput Experiments' (ACS Sustain. Chem. Eng., doi 10.1021/acssuschemeng.4c06166).

sources.system: Automated Pb-212/Bi-212 radioisotope generator production platform
sources.title: PNNL Producing Cancer-Fighting Radioisotopes to Help Research Better, Faster Cures | PNNL
sources.claim: PNNL developed and operates a fully automated radiochemical platform that processes radium/lead/bismuth radioisotopes and assembles Pb-212/Bi-212 generators, i.e., machine-executed handling of highly radioactive solutions and separation chemistry in shielded enclosures.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated radiochemical processing/separation of highly radioactive solutions. Transfers to bench radiochemical experiments in that the liquids, containment and precision of transfers/separations are the same, though the platform runs a fixed process rather than an exploratory campaign.

May specialize in electrical systems; heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning (HVAC) systems; green buildings; lighting; air quality; or energy procurement.

tasks.label: Collect data for energy conservation analyses, using jobsite observation, field inspections, or sub-metering.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: One-off walk-through audit (ASHRAE Level I/II style) of a commercial or institutional building (office, school, hospital, retail) the engineer has not visited before: touring floors, mechanical and electrical rooms and the roof; recording nameplate data on chillers, boilers, rooftop units and pumps; counting and typing lighting fixtures; reading thermostat/BAS setpoints; taking spot measurements (clamp-meter amps, temperatures, light levels); photographing conditions and noting operating schedules.

Recurring energy field survey inside an industrial or manufacturing plant the engineer supports: ultrasonic/acoustic compressed-air and gas leak survey along production lines, thermal scans of motors, pumps, gearboxes and steam lines, and readings of pressure/flow gauges and panel indicators at known assets, logged for trend and savings analysis.

Short-term sub-metering / monitoring deployment: clamping current transformers onto conductors inside live electrical panels, wiring and mounting power loggers, placing temperature/humidity/light/runtime loggers on equipment and in occupied spaces, verifying readings and communications, then returning weeks later to retrieve devices and download data.

Scheduled monitoring rounds through a large fixed-asset facility (data center whitespace and cooling plant, central utility plant, substation/converter station) capturing thermal images of equipment, space temperatures and gauge/indicator readings on a repeatable route to feed efficiency and energy-trend analysis.

Jobsite observation on an active construction or major retrofit site: walking the site to observe and document installed conditions relevant to energy performance (whether specified HVAC equipment, ductwork, insulation, glazing and envelope details are installed as designed), capturing photos/scans and flagging deviations from design for the energy analysis, amid unfinished floors, working trades, debris and changing layout.

Residential or small multifamily audit: whole-dwelling field inspection with a blower-door air-leakage test, infrared scan of walls and ceilings, attic and crawlspace inspection, combustion-appliance checks and inventory of equipment and appliances, in an occupied private home.

tasks.label: Conduct energy audits to evaluate energy use and to identify conservation and cost reduction measures.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ASHRAE Level 1/2 audit of an occupied commercial office or retail building: walk tenant floors, mechanical and electrical rooms, and the roof; inventory nameplate data on RTUs, chillers, pumps and lighting; take light-level, temperature and clamp-on amp readings; set temporary data loggers; interview the facility manager; pull BAS trends and 12-24 months of utility bills; deliver a report of energy conservation measures with savings, cost and payback.

Industrial/manufacturing plant audit (DOE Industrial Assessment Center style): survey compressed air for leaks and pressure/flow, log motor, pump and fan loads on live switchgear, run combustion analysis on boilers, check steam traps and process heat recovery, tour hot/noisy production areas with the plant engineer, then quantify measures and payback for production-constrained operations.

Institutional campus, hospital or K-12 school audit with a central plant: inspect chillers, boilers, cooling towers, AHUs and distribution; verify schedules, setpoints and economizer/VAV operation against BAS trends; access occupied clinical/classroom spaces under escort and infection-control or security restrictions; report prioritized ECMs and utility incentive eligibility.

Residential or small multifamily audit: blower door and duct leakage testing, combustion safety and CO testing on furnace/water heater, infrared scan of walls and ceilings, inspection of attic, basement and crawlspace insulation, homeowner interview on comfort and bills, followed by a prioritized weatherization/equipment recommendation list.

Utility-program screening audits across many small commercial sites (restaurants, convenience stores, small shops): short walkthrough of cluttered back-of-house, kitchens and cellars; count and identify lighting fixtures and refrigeration cases; spot-check controls; scope direct-install measures and produce a same-day findings sheet for the customer and program administrator.

sources.title: Thermal Sensing & Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics' Spot with the Spot CAM+IR payload runs pre-planned autonomous inspection rounds in industrial facilities, capturing thermal scans of designated assets and trending temperatures for predictive maintenance.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: routine thermal inspection rounds in plants. It transfers only partially to energy auditing: it supplies one data-collection sub-step (IR imagery of pre-taught asset points on a fixed route) but not equipment inventory, electrical/flow metering, occupant interviews, or the engineering analysis that constitutes an audit.

sources.title: Acoustic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Spot equipped with acoustic imaging payloads automates ultrasonic scanning of rotating equipment and compressed-air systems, locating pinhole air leaks in industrial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: compressed-air leak surveying, a recognized sub-step of an industrial energy audit. Objects (air lines, bearings) and setting (plant floor) match, but a leak list is a fraction of an audit's scope and deliverable.

sources.system: Fluke SV600 acoustic imager on Spot
sources.title: Advanced Robotics and Acoustic Imaging | Fluke Process Instruments
sources.claim: Fluke's SV600 acoustic imager, when mounted on a mobile robot, continuously scans plant areas for air and gas leaks and mechanical anomalies, automating acoustic inspection routes.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: automated leak detection in industrial facilities; covers one measurement sub-step of an energy audit only, and the level of robot autonomy in the pairing is not established in the source.

sources.title: ANYbotics launches Gas Leak and Presence Detection for ANYmal inspection robot - The Robot Report
sources.claim: ANYbotics' ANYmal legged inspection robot gained an acoustic payload for detecting industrial gas and compressed-air/steam leaks during autonomous inspection missions in plants.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: autonomous industrial inspection rounds. Shows mobile robots can traverse structured plants and sense leaks, but not that they can perform an audit's metering, inventory, interview and analysis steps.

sources.title: RoboAuditor: Goal-Oriented Robotic System for Assessing Energy-intensive Indoor Appliance via Visual Language Models
sources.claim: RoboAuditor, the closest published attempt at a robotic energy-audit system, autonomously navigates to identify and localize energy-intensive appliances, but was evaluated only in 3D simulation of residential buildings and covers only appliance identification.
sources.transferJustification: Directly related task (robotic energy auditing), but simulation-only and limited to locating appliances, so it cannot substantiate completion of a real audit in any environment.

sources.system: Zeitview Property Insights Platform (aerial thermal analysis)
sources.title: Zeitview Expands Rooftop Inspection Capacity with AI-Enabled Software Platform and Aerial Thermal Analysis
sources.claim: Drone-based rooftop and facade thermal inspection services with AI analytics are sold commercially to find moisture and energy-loss areas on buildings; flights are pilot-operated capture missions delivering imagery and anomaly reports, not full energy audits.
sources.transferJustification: Related task: building-envelope thermography, a sub-step of an energy audit. Autonomy of the capture flights is not established and the service does not deliver equipment inventory, interior measurements, or ECM economics.

tasks.label: Perform energy modeling, measurement, verification, commissioning, or retro-commissioning.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: Whole-building or process energy modeling at the desk: building/calibrating a simulation model (eQUEST, EnergyPlus, IES-VE, TRACE) from drawings, nameplate data and utility bills, running parametric ECM runs, and documenting results for code/LEED/incentive submittals. Office work at a computer; no physical manipulation of equipment.

Commissioning of a new construction or major-retrofit project: executing/witnessing functional performance tests on AHUs, VAVs, chillers, boilers, pumps and controls in a building at substantial completion. Involves ladder and roof access, opening panels and mechanical-room equipment, forcing BAS points, taking airflow/temperature/amperage readings with hand instruments, and logging deficiencies while trades work around you.

Retro-commissioning investigation in an existing occupied facility (hospital, university campus, office tower): field survey of air handlers, VAV boxes, dampers, valves and sensors; checking sensor calibration against handheld references; running functional tests coordinated with facility staff during off-hours; combined with BAS trend review to produce a findings/savings report.

Measurement & verification field instrumentation: installing and later retrieving portable metering 	ersered clamp-on CTs and power loggers inside live electrical panels, lighting loggers, temperature/runtime/pressure loggers on equipment 	ers in an existing commercial or institutional building, then performing IPMVP Option A/B/C analysis and issuing the savings report.

Recurring plant-wide loss measurement rounds inside an industrial facility: walking fixed routes through the plant to capture thermal images of motors, electrical gear and steam/heat equipment and ultrasonic/acoustic scans of compressed-air and steam distribution, locating and quantifying leaks/losses, and feeding findings into the site's asset/energy management system for repair prioritization.

Other industrial field measurements for an energy study: flue-gas combustion analysis with a probe in the boiler stack, contact ultrasonic/temperature steam-trap testing, temporary power logging on motors and compressors, and pump/fan head-flow measurements, performed during a plant energy assessment.

tasks.label: Inspect or monitor energy systems, including heating, ventilating, and air conditioning (HVAC) or daylighting systems to determine energy use or potential energy savings.

automationEvidence.assessmentType: Published AI-assisted research assessment; not an independently observed task trial

instances.label: ASHRAE Level 1/2 walkthrough audit of a commercial building (office, school, retail): engineer tours mechanical rooms, roofs and rooftop units, above-ceiling plenums and electrical rooms; opens AHU/RTU access panels; records nameplate and control-setpoint data; spot-measures airflow, temperatures, illuminance and daylight availability; photographs and thermally images equipment and envelope; produces an energy-use breakdown and savings-opportunity list.

Recurring inspection/monitoring rounds of energy systems at an institution-controlled facility (manufacturing plant, central utility plant, refinery, data center): fixed routes past compressors, pumps, motors, boilers, chillers and CRAC units capturing thermal images, analog/digital gauge and meter readings, and ultrasonic/acoustic surveys for compressed-air and steam leaks, trended into a monitoring platform with anomalies and energy waste flagged for follow-up.

Full industrial energy assessment using contact instrumentation: ultrasonic/temperature testing of steam traps, clamp-on power and amperage logging on motors and feeders, stack combustion analysis on boilers, flow and pressure measurement on compressed-air headers, plus operator interviews, culminating in a quantified savings-measure report.

Deploying and retrieving portable measurement equipment for a monitoring campaign: opening live electrical panels to clamp current transformers, installing power/temperature/light data loggers and occupancy sensors around a facility, verifying BAS/EMS sensor readings against handheld instruments, then collecting the devices weeks later.

Residential or small-commercial energy audit: blower-door depressurization test, duct leakage test, infrared scan of walls and ceilings, attic and crawlspace insulation inspection, furnace/water-heater combustion safety check, in an occupied home taken as found (clutter, pets, varied layouts).

sources.title: Acoustic Inspection | Boston Dynamics
sources.claim: Boston Dynamics sells and supports autonomous acoustic inspection routes with Spot carrying the Fluke SV600, detecting compressed-air/gas leaks and noise anomalies on scheduled missions inside industrial facilities.
sources.transferJustification: Compressed-air leak surveying is a standard energy-waste inspection; the same page cites DOE per-leak cost figures, so the captured output is an energy-loss determination of the kind this task requires.

sources.title: ANYmal X Tested for Autonomous Robot Inspections in Ex-zones at BASF
sources.claim: ANYmal X runs autonomous multi-floor inspection missions at BASF Ludwigshafen, reading gauges, liquid levels and lever positions and taking thermal images of tanks and pumps while trending anomaly data.
sources.transferJustification: Thermal imaging of pumps and vessels plus instrument readings on fixed routes is the equipment-condition and energy-loss monitoring an engineer would otherwise walk manually.

sources.transferJustification: Temperature and equipment monitoring rounds in data halls are cooling-system monitoring of the kind an energy engineer performs to find thermal and airflow inefficiency.

sources.transferJustification: Directly this task (robotic energy auditing of indoor appliances and HVAC); cited to show the indoor-audit state of the art falls short of completing an audit.
